title: The secret of Chidambaram
hookLine: a priest draws back a curtain beside the dancer at Chidambaram, and behind it: the same lord, without form
carry: the same lord, with form and as open space
tomorrow: why does Shiva have a thousand names?
last: SHE CAME DOWN TO SET SOULS FREE.

lines: A HALL WITH A GOLDEN ROOF.
cards: At Chidambaram, in Tamil Nadu, the dancing Shiva isn't in a museum case. He stands in a hall with a golden roof, dressed, garlanded, bathed and sung to, while a crowd presses forward and oil lamps are waved in the dark.

Temple tradition says this is where he danced for two sages who longed to see it: Patanjali, shown with the body of a serpent, and Vyaghrapada, whose name means tiger-foot. And beside the dancer hangs a curtain.
At certain moments a priest draws it back, and the people lean in.

teach.b: Behind the curtain there seems to be nothing: an empty space, hung with a garland of golden bilva leaves. It's called the Chidambara rahasya, the secret of Chidambaram.
The dancer is there in form, with arms and hair and fire. And right beside him, the same lord, with no form at all. Space.

Tradition links this temple with space itself, the open sky the dance happens in. Now put the whole image back together, because a Shaiva teaching does exactly that. It reads the dance as doing five things at once.
The drum: creation. The raised hand that says do not fear: preservation, keeping what's made. The flame: dissolution.
The planted foot on Apasmara: concealment, the veil of forgetting that hides what's true. And the lifted foot the elephant hand points to: grace, release.

teach.h: FIVE ACTS: MAKE, KEEP, END, HIDE, FREE.
teach.b: Make, keep, end, hide, free: five acts, one dancer, never stopping. And then the curtain opens on the space beside him.
This is a teaching Hindus live with every day: God with form and God beyond form are not two gods.
So a grandmother can bathe and dress an image with real tenderness, and say in the same breath that God is everywhere and no image holds him. The secret isn't locked away.
It's shown, on purpose, to anyone standing in the crowd.

teach.h: THE SAME LORD, WITH FORM AND AS SPACE.
teach.b: The tradition doesn't ask anyone to choose between the dancer and the empty space. It keeps them side by side, behind one curtain.

how: At the Nataraja temple in Chidambaram, Tamil Nadu, the dancing Shiva is worshiped daily with lamps, bathing and song, and priests at times draw back a curtain to show the Chidambara rahasya, an empty space hung with golden bilva leaves.

a temple curtain that hides the god from the crowd

games.q: you're in the crowd at Chidambaram. the priest draws back the curtain beside the dancer. what do you see?
o: a second image of Shiva, covered in jewels.
an empty space, hung with golden bilva leaves.
games.why: the Chidambara rahasya: the same lord, without form, shown on purpose beside the dancer with form.

practice: If there's an image of God near you, a picture, a statue, a lamp, look at it for a few breaths with care, the way a devotee looks at the dancer.
Then close your eyes and notice the space around you, the quiet behind the sounds, and rest there, holding the image and the space together without choosing.
If you pray, say Shiva's name, or the name of God you use, into that space; if not, just rest in it.

wordCard.voice: Nataraja, whole: five acts in one dance, and beside him at Chidambaram, an empty space that is the same lord without form.

orig.note: Sanskrit form of the temple's name, read in tradition as the sky of consciousness; the town is Chidambaram in Tamil Nadu.

carryVoice: Your line: the same lord, with form and as open space. Bow to the image, and know he fills the room. Until tomorrow.
